newsitem.title: UK: FTSE 100 ends at a new record high.
newsitem.headline: FTSE 100 ends at a new record high.

text.p: Leading UK blue chips finished at another record peak on Wednesday, buoyed by a better performance on Wall Street, a successful gilts auction, and renewed bid speculation.
Several waves of index-arbitrage related buying provided additional support and helped bolster otherwise thin volume, registering only 551.2 million shares by 1544 GMT.
The FTSE 100 closed 13.0 points higher at 3,918.7, after setting a record at 3,922.1. Advancers beat decliners by a margin on five to three.
A firmer U.S. market overnight helped establish the stronger tone at the start, traders said.
The auction of 2.5 billion stg of ten-year 7.5 percent gilts, covered 2.69 times, boosted the gilts market, which in turn helped whisk UK shares higher, traders said.
"The Street is strong, bonds are up, gilts are up and Japanese rates don't look set to go higher...All of these little things are just slowly pushing (UK shares) higher," said one.

Bid speculation, meanwhile, re-emerged in the financial sector. Lloyds Abbey Life shares surged 32-1/2p to 593p amid rumours that Prudential, which announced the sale of its Mercantile & General unit, wanted to bid for the company.
Analysts said Lloyds TSB Group is a more likely bidder for life insurer Lloyds Abbey than Prudential. Lloyds TSB already has a 62 percent stake in the life insurer.
Neither Prudential nor Lloyds would comment on the talk.
The broad market, traders said, is unlikely to move significantly higher unless some of the bids rumoured around the market begin to materialise.
"Either that, or we have to see better profits or lower interest rates, said another trader.
UBS equity strategist Scott Evan pegs the relative value of the FTSE 100 between 3,800 and 3,900.
"Anything above 3,900 is overvalued because nothing has really changed recently," said Evans.

The FTSE 100, up about 6.5 percent during the past month, has risen to record levels on low trading volume during this traditional summer holiday season. The lack of turnover during the most recent advance has made many marketwatchers skeptical about the sustainability of the rally.
A total of 562 million shares registered by 1600 GMT.
"Trading volumes are low, so it's difficult to gauge what sentiment really is," said Evan. "The test will be in September, when everyone is back and we get more interim results."
Shares in WH Smith fell 6p to 509-1/2p as traders took profits on an initial rise after the company reported a pre-tax loss of 194.7 million stg.
Shares in Allied Domecq added 13p to 466-1/2p as Kleinwort Benson upgraded the stock to a "buy" from a "hold."
"(Volume) seems to be concentrated in a few select shares," said a trader.
Better-than-expected UK trade figures had little impact on equities.
The non-EU July trade deficit totalled 506 million stg while June's world deficit was 1.12 billion stg.

"The July figures are pretty encouraging, certainly much better than had been expected. They tend to suggest that there's been some improvement in the export outlook which was what the CBI seemed to be suggesting in their quarterly survey," said BankAmerica economist Rob Hayward.
